rules.title: ProgramData
rules.summary: Machine-wide data of Windows and installed programs; check each folder
rules.whatItIs: Hidden folder where Windows and programs keep data shared by all users: settings, licenses, databases, caches, installer caches and update downloads.
rules.whyBig: Installer caches (Package Cache), game launcher data, antivirus definitions, the search index and app databases.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs and Windows features that keep data here break; some lose licenses or must be reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Check each subfolder; vendor folders of programs you uninstalled are reported as possible leftovers.

rules.title: Windows machine-wide data
rules.summary: Machine-wide data of Windows and Microsoft components
rules.whatItIs: Data of Windows itself shared by all users: Defender, the search index, error reports, crypto keys, device setup, Windows Update orchestration and more.
rules.whyBig: Defender definitions, the search index and error reports are the usual large parts; they are explained separately.
rules.ifDeleted: Windows components break; some failures only show up later (sign-in, encryption, updates).
rules.saferAlternative: Clean only the parts marked SAFE (Error Reporting) or shrink the search index from Indexing Options.

rules.title: Start menu (all users)
rules.summary: Start menu shortcuts installed for all users
rules.whatItIs: Shortcuts that programs installed for everyone put in the Start menu.
rules.whyBig: Tiny; shortcuts only.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs disappear from the Start menu but stay installed.

rules.title: Hyper-V virtual machine configuration
rules.summary: Hyper-V VM configurations and saved states
rules.whatItIs: Default folder for Hyper-V virtual machine configuration files, saved states and checkpoint data.
rules.whyBig: Saved VM states are as large as the VM's memory.
rules.ifDeleted: Virtual machines disappear from Hyper-V Manager or fail to start.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete VMs and checkpoints in Hyper-V Manager.

rules.title: Hyper-V virtual hard disks
rules.summary: Default location of Hyper-V virtual disks on Windows 10/11
rules.whatItIs: Hyper-V on Windows 10 and 11 stores new virtual hard disks (.vhdx) here by default.
rules.whyBig: Each disk grows to the data stored in its virtual machine.
rules.ifDeleted: The virtual machines lose their disks and everything inside them.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete VMs in Hyper-V Manager, then remove their disks.

rules.title: Installer package cache
rules.summary: Cached installers needed to repair, upgrade or uninstall programs
rules.whatItIs: Installer bundles built with WiX Burn (Visual C++ runtimes, .NET, Visual Studio components, many SDKs and games) cache their setup packages here so they can repair, change or remove the program later.
rules.whyBig: Every bundle keeps its packages, and versions of frequently updated runtimes add up to several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: The programs keep running, but repairing, upgrading or uninstalling them can fail or ask for the original installer. Visual C++ runtime updates are a common victim.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall programs you do not need; their cached packages are removed with them. Do not delete folders by hand.

rules.title: Visual Studio installer cache
rules.summary: Visual Studio installer packages; can be turned off, then downloaded on demand
rules.whatItIs: Package cache of the Visual Studio Installer, used to repair or modify Visual Studio without downloading.
rules.whyBig: It keeps the packages of every installed workload and component, often several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Visual Studio keeps working; repairs, updates and changes download what they need again.
rules.saferAlternative: Microsoft documents a 'KeepDownloadedPayloads' policy (or the --nocache install option) to stop caching; with it set, the installer removes cached packages.

rules.title: Update orchestrator data (private)
rules.summary: Windows Update orchestrator state
rules.whatItIs: Private data of the Update Session Orchestrator, the service that schedules Windows Update scans, downloads and restarts.
rules.whyBig: Small.
rules.ifDeleted: Windows Update scheduling can break.

rules.title: Update orchestrator data (shared)
rules.summary: Windows Update orchestrator logs and shared state
rules.whatItIs: Logs and shared data of the Update Session Orchestrator.
rules.whyBig: Logs rotate; usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Windows Update scheduling can break.

rules.title: OpenSSH server configuration
rules.summary: OpenSSH server settings and host keys
rules.whatItIs: Configuration and host keys of the Windows OpenSSH server, created when the server feature is installed or first started.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: The SSH server loses its settings and host keys; clients see a host key change warning.

rules.title: Software identification tags
rules.summary: Software identification tags used for license and inventory tracking
rules.whatItIs: ISO software identification (SWID) tags that vendors such as Microsoft and Adobe write so inventory and license tools can recognise installed products.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Inventory and licensing tools may no longer recognise the installed products.

rules.title: OneDrive (machine-wide)
rules.summary: Machine-wide OneDrive setup data
rules.whatItIs: Data of OneDrive when it is installed for all users.
rules.whyBig: Small.
rules.ifDeleted: OneDrive setup and updates may fail.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Application Data
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to ProgramData.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Desktop
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to the public desktop.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Documents
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to the public documents.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Start Menu
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to the all-users Start menu.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Templates
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to the all-users templates.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: NVIDIA machine-wide data
rules.summary: NVIDIA driver and app data: settings, downloads and installer files
rules.whatItIs: Machine-wide data of NVIDIA drivers and software: driver settings (DRS), downloaded driver updates, installer files and SDK data.
rules.whyBig: Downloaded driver packages and installer leftovers are the usual large parts.
rules.ifDeleted: Driver settings and NVIDIA software break; the driver itself stays installed.

rules.title: NVIDIA driver downloads
rules.summary: Driver updates downloaded by the NVIDIA app or GeForce Experience
rules.whatItIs: Driver packages that the NVIDIA app or GeForce Experience downloaded for installation.
rules.whyBig: Each driver download is several hundred MB to over 1 GB, and old ones can stay.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; a driver that was not installed yet is downloaded again.

rules.title: NVIDIA installer files
rules.summary: Installer copies of NVIDIA driver components
rules.whatItIs: Files the NVIDIA installer keeps for installed driver components.
rules.whyBig: Older driver installers left copies for each version, which could reach several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: The current driver keeps working, but changing or removing NVIDIA components may fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Run a clean driver install with the NVIDIA installer, which removes outdated packages.

rules.title: NVIDIA shader cache (older drivers)
rules.summary: Shader cache used by older NVIDIA drivers; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Compiled shader cache of older NVIDIA drivers.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; shaders are recompiled, with stutter at first.

rules.title: Docker Windows containers data
rules.summary: Images and containers of Docker's Windows containers mode; prune, do not delete
rules.whatItIs: Data root of Docker when it runs Windows containers: images, container layers, volumes and build cache.
rules.whyBig: Windows base images are several GB each, and every pulled image and stopped container adds layers.
rules.ifDeleted: Docker's state is corrupted; images, containers and volumes (including their data) are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'docker system prune' to remove stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images and build cache. Add '-a' to remove all unused images and '--volumes' only if you are sure no volume holds needed data.

rules.title: Chocolatey package manager
rules.summary: Chocolatey and the packages it installed
rules.whatItIs: The Chocolatey package manager: its program, package metadata (lib), shims (bin) and logs.
rules.whyBig: Portable packages live entirely in lib; logs grow over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Chocolatey and portable packages stop working; programs it installed normally stay but can no longer be managed by it.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall packages with 'choco uninstall <name>'.

rules.title: Epic Games machine-wide data
rules.summary: Epic Games Launcher manifests and shared data
rules.whatItIs: Machine-wide data of the Epic Games Launcher, including the manifests that record which games are installed where.
rules.whyBig: Small; manifests and launcher data.
rules.ifDeleted: The launcher forgets which games are installed and may offer to download them again.

rules.title: Battle.net agent
rules.summary: Battle.net Agent, which installs and updates Blizzard games
rules.whatItIs: The Battle.net Agent and its data, used to install, update and repair Blizzard games.
rules.whyBig: Agent versions and logs, usually a few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Battle.net reinstalls the agent on next start; Blizzard's own troubleshooting deletes this folder.

rules.title: Blizzard shared data
rules.summary: Shared data of the Battle.net app and Blizzard games
rules.whatItIs: Machine-wide data of the Battle.net app and Blizzard games.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Battle.net may need to repair itself.

rules.title: Riot Games shared data
rules.summary: Shared data of the Riot Client and Riot games
rules.whatItIs: Machine-wide data of the Riot Client, including install metadata for Riot games.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: The Riot Client may lose track of installed games and need repair.

rules.title: Unity machine-wide data
rules.summary: Unity licensing and machine-wide editor data
rules.whatItIs: Machine-wide data of Unity: licensing client configuration and shared editor data.
rules.whyBig: Small.
rules.ifDeleted: Unity may need to be re-activated.

rules.title: Program Files
rules.summary: Installed 64-bit programs; remove them with their uninstaller
rules.whatItIs: Default install location for 64-bit programs installed for all users, plus Windows components such as Windows Defender and WindowsApps.
rules.whyBig: Games, creative suites, SDKs and engines are the usual large parts.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting a program's folder leaves broken shortcuts, registry entries and services behind; the program has to be reinstalled before it can be uninstalled cleanly.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall programs from Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

rules.title: Program Files (x86)
rules.summary: Installed 32-bit programs (and some launchers); remove them with their uninstaller
rules.whatItIs: Default install location for 32-bit programs, and for some 64-bit apps whose installers still choose it (Steam, many launchers and SDKs).
rules.whyBig: Steam and its games, Windows SDKs and Visual Studio components are often large.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting a program's folder leaves it half-installed; it has to be reinstalled before it can be removed cleanly.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall programs from Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

rules.title: Common Files (shared components)
rules.summary: Components shared by several programs; removed by their uninstallers
rules.whatItIs: Libraries and components that programs share, such as Microsoft Shared (Office, VSTO), Adobe, Apple and audio plug-in folders (VST3).
rules.whyBig: Office shared components and plug-in folders can be several hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs that rely on these shared parts stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall the programs that installed them.

rules.title: Common Files (x86, shared components)
rules.summary: 32-bit components shared by several programs
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit libraries and components shared by programs, such as Microsoft Shared and vendor runtimes.
rules.whyBig: Usually a few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs that rely on these shared parts stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall the programs that installed them.

rules.title: Microsoft Defender program files
rules.summary: Microsoft Defender Antivirus program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of Microsoft Defender Antivirus, part of Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Defender for Endpoint sensor
rules.summary: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint components
rules.whatItIs: Components of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (the enterprise sensor), part of Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Microsoft Defender (32-bit parts)
rules.summary: 32-bit parts of Microsoft Defender
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit components of Microsoft Defender Antivirus, part of Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Mail components
rules.summary: Built-in Windows mail components
rules.whatItIs: Components that ship with Windows for mail and contacts support.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Mail components (32-bit)
rules.summary: Built-in Windows mail components (32-bit)
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit components that ship with Windows for mail and contacts support.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Media Player (legacy)
rules.summary: Built-in Windows Media Player program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of the legacy Windows Media Player, a Windows feature.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Media Player (legacy, 32-bit)
rules.summary: Built-in Windows Media Player program files (32-bit)
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit program files of the legacy Windows Media Player.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows NT accessories
rules.summary: Built-in Windows accessories (WordPad, Paint parts, TAPI)
rules.whatItIs: Accessories and components that ship with Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows NT accessories (32-bit)
rules.summary: Built-in Windows accessories (32-bit)
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit accessories and components that ship with Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Photo Viewer
rules.summary: Built-in legacy Windows Photo Viewer
rules.whatItIs: Program files of the legacy Windows Photo Viewer.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Photo Viewer (32-bit)
rules.summary: Built-in legacy Windows Photo Viewer (32-bit)
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit program files of the legacy Windows Photo Viewer.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Sidebar (legacy)
rules.summary: Leftover gadget platform folder from older Windows
rules.whatItIs: Folder of the old desktop gadgets platform that Windows still ships for compatibility.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows Sidebar (legacy, 32-bit)
rules.summary: Leftover gadget platform folder from older Windows
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit folder of the old desktop gadgets platform kept for compatibility.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows PowerShell modules
rules.summary: Modules for Windows PowerShell (all users)
rules.whatItIs: Modules installed for Windows PowerShell for all users, including ones that ship with Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Windows PowerShell modules (32-bit)
rules.summary: Modules for 32-bit Windows PowerShell
rules.whatItIs: Modules for 32-bit Windows PowerShell for all users.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Internet Explorer components
rules.summary: Internet Explorer components kept for IE mode and old apps
rules.whatItIs: Components of Internet Explorer that Windows keeps for Edge's IE mode and old apps.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Internet Explorer components (32-bit)
rules.summary: 32-bit Internet Explorer components
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit components of Internet Explorer kept by Windows.
rules.whyBig: Part of Windows; its size changes only with Windows updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Built-in Windows features or apps that depend on it stop working, and Windows Update may fail to service it.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off unused optional features in Settings > System > Optional features instead.

rules.title: Moddable Store games
rules.summary: Store and Xbox games installed with a moddable folder
rules.whatItIs: Some Microsoft Store and Xbox app games install here so that their files can be modified (mods).
rules.whyBig: Each game is tens of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: The games stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall them from the Xbox app or Installed apps.

rules.title: Uninstall Information (legacy)
rules.summary: Legacy uninstall data of old Windows components
rules.whatItIs: Data kept by older Windows component installers so they could be removed later.
rules.whyBig: Usually tiny or empty.
rules.ifDeleted: Old components may not uninstall; there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: .NET runtimes and SDKs
rules.summary: .NET runtimes and SDKs used by apps and developers; old versions pile up
rules.whatItIs: The machine-wide .NET installation: shared runtimes (shared), SDKs (sdk), workloads and templates. Apps built on .NET 5+ run on these runtimes.
rules.whyBig: Each SDK is several hundred MB and Visual Studio or Windows Update installs new ones without removing old ones.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps that need a removed runtime fail to start, and builds fail without the SDK they target.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'dotnet --list-sdks' to see versions, and remove old ones from Installed apps or with Microsoft's .NET Uninstall Tool.

rules.title: .NET runtimes (32-bit)
rules.summary: 32-bit .NET runtimes used by 32-bit apps
rules.whatItIs: The 32-bit .NET installation used by 32-bit apps built on .NET 5+.
rules.whyBig: Each runtime is tens of MB; old versions stay.
rules.ifDeleted: 32-bit .NET apps fail to start.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove old runtimes from Installed apps.

rules.title: Reference assemblies
rules.summary: Reference assemblies used to build .NET Framework apps
rules.whatItIs: Reference assemblies that Visual Studio and MSBuild use to compile against specific .NET Framework versions.
rules.whyBig: One set per targeting pack, tens to hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds that target those framework versions fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove targeting packs with the Visual Studio Installer.

rules.title: Reference assemblies (x86)
rules.summary: Reference assemblies used to build .NET Framework apps
rules.whatItIs: Reference assemblies and .NET Framework targeting packs used by Visual Studio and MSBuild.
rules.whyBig: One set per targeting pack, up to several hundred MB in total.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds that target those framework versions fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove targeting packs with the Visual Studio Installer.

rules.title: MSBuild extensions
rules.summary: Shared MSBuild targets and extensions
rules.whatItIs: Build targets and extensions shared by Visual Studio and SDKs.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds that import these targets fail.

rules.title: MSBuild extensions (x86)
rules.summary: Shared MSBuild targets and extensions
rules.whatItIs: Build targets and extensions shared by Visual Studio and SDKs.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds that import these targets fail.

rules.title: Windows SDKs and kits
rules.summary: Windows SDK, WDK and debugging tools; remove old SDK versions
rules.whatItIs: Windows Software Development Kits, the Driver Kit, debugging tools and the Windows App Certification Kit, installed by Visual Studio or separately.
rules.whyBig: Each SDK version is 1-3 GB, and Visual Studio adds new ones without removing old ones.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds that target removed SDK versions fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall old 'Windows Software Development Kit' entries in Installed apps or via the Visual Studio Installer.

rules.title: Microsoft SDKs
rules.summary: SDKs and tools for Windows, .NET, Azure and NuGet fallback packages
rules.whatItIs: SDK components installed by Visual Studio: Windows and .NET tools, Azure SDKs and offline NuGet packages.
rules.whyBig: Several SDKs and offline package folders add up.
rules.ifDeleted: Builds and tools that depend on them fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove components with the Visual Studio Installer.

rules.title: .NET Framework SDK tools
rules.summary: .NET Framework SDK tools and targeting data
rules.whatItIs: Tools and data from .NET Framework SDKs and targeting packs.
rules.whyBig: Usually modest.
rules.ifDeleted: Development tools that rely on them fail.

rules.title: Visual Studio
rules.summary: Visual Studio installations; change or remove them with the Visual Studio Installer
rules.whatItIs: Visual Studio IDE installations (one folder per year and edition) with their workloads, compilers and tools.
rules.whyBig: A typical installation is 10-40 GB depending on workloads (C++, game development and Android add a lot).
rules.ifDeleted: Visual Studio breaks and the installer can no longer update or remove it cleanly.
rules.saferAlternative: Open the Visual Studio Installer and remove workloads or whole installations you do not use.

rules.title: Visual Studio Installer and shared parts
rules.summary: Visual Studio Installer and components shared between Visual Studio versions
rules.whatItIs: The Visual Studio Installer and shared components (Shared folder) used by all installed Visual Studio versions, plus older installations.
rules.whyBig: Shared components and older Visual Studio versions can be several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Visual Studio can no longer be updated, modified or uninstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Use the Visual Studio Installer to remove what you do not need.

rules.title: Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
rules.summary: Web runtime used by many apps (Teams, Office, widgets); do not delete
rules.whatItIs: The WebView2 Runtime that apps use to show web content: new Teams, Outlook, Office features, Windows widgets and many third-party apps.
rules.whyBig: Each version is several hundred MB, and an update keeps the previous version until it is no longer in use.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps that rely on WebView2 show blank windows or fail to start.
rules.saferAlternative: Leave it; it updates itself.

rules.title: Microsoft Edge program files
rules.summary: Microsoft Edge browser program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of the Microsoft Edge browser.
rules.whyBig: Each version is several hundred MB; the previous version stays until the update completes.
rules.ifDeleted: Edge stops working, and Windows features and links that open Edge fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Leave it; Edge is part of Windows and repairs itself through updates.

rules.title: Microsoft Office
rules.summary: Microsoft Office / Microsoft 365 apps; repair or remove via Installed apps
rules.whatItIs: Microsoft Office or Microsoft 365 apps. Click-to-Run installs keep the apps in the root subfolder.
rules.whyBig: A full Microsoft 365 install is 3-5 GB, plus extra languages and Visio or Project.
rules.ifDeleted: Office breaks and can no longer be repaired or updated; it has to be removed with Microsoft's support tool and reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove Office or change languages from Installed apps.

rules.title: Office Click-to-Run client
rules.summary: Office Click-to-Run integration files
rules.whatItIs: Integration components of Office Click-to-Run, used to install, update and stream Office apps.
rules.whyBig: A few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Office updates and repairs fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove Office from Installed apps if you no longer use it.

rules.title: NVIDIA software
rules.summary: NVIDIA driver components, control panel and the NVIDIA app
rules.whatItIs: Program files of NVIDIA driver components and software: control panel, NVIDIA app or GeForce Experience, PhysX, audio and installer.
rules.whyBig: Several hundred MB to a few GB, depending on installed components.
rules.ifDeleted: Graphics settings, the NVIDIA app and parts of the driver stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove components from Installed apps or reinstall the driver with a clean installation.

rules.title: NVIDIA software (32-bit)
rules.summary: 32-bit NVIDIA components such as PhysX
rules.whatItIs: 32-bit components of NVIDIA software, for example the PhysX runtime.
rules.whyBig: Usually a few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Games that use these components may fail.

rules.title: AMD software
rules.summary: AMD Software (Adrenalin), chipset utilities and Ryzen Master
rules.whatItIs: Program files of AMD software: the Adrenalin graphics app, chipset tools and Ryzen Master.
rules.whyBig: Usually 1-2 GB.
rules.ifDeleted: AMD Software and its settings stop working; the driver may lose features.

rules.title: Docker Desktop program files
rules.summary: Docker Desktop program files; your images live elsewhere
rules.whatItIs: Program files of Docker Desktop. Images and containers are stored in its virtual disk (see AppData\Local\Docker).
rules.whyBig: Docker Desktop is a few GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Docker Desktop stops working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall from Installed apps.

rules.title: Meta Quest Link (Oculus) app
rules.summary: Meta Quest Link / Oculus PC app and its game library
rules.whatItIs: The Meta Quest Link (formerly Oculus) PC app; by default it also stores downloaded VR games under Software.
rules.whyBig: VR games are several GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: The app and its VR games stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from the app's library and the app from Installed apps.

rules.title: Meta Quest Link game library
rules.summary: VR games downloaded through the Meta Quest Link (Oculus) app
rules.whatItIs: Default library folder of the Meta Quest Link app, with downloaded VR games.
rules.whyBig: VR games are several GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: The games stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from the Meta Quest Link app's library.

rules.title: Unity editors (installed by Unity Hub)
rules.summary: Unity editor versions installed by Unity Hub; remove old ones from the Hub
rules.whatItIs: Every Unity editor version installed through Unity Hub, with its platform build support modules.
rules.whyBig: Each editor is 5-15 GB with build support (Android, iOS, WebGL), and installing a new version keeps the old ones.
rules.ifDeleted: Projects that use a removed version must be opened with another version (which can require upgrading them).
rules.saferAlternative: In Unity Hub > Installs, uninstall versions no projects use any more.

rules.title: Unity
rules.summary: Unity editors and Unity Hub content
rules.whatItIs: Unity editors installed directly or through Unity Hub (Hub\Editor).
rules.whyBig: Each editor version is several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Unity editors stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Manage installs in Unity Hub.

rules.title: Unity Hub
rules.summary: Unity Hub program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of Unity Hub, the launcher that installs and manages Unity editors.
rules.whyBig: A few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Unity Hub stops working; installed editors stay.

rules.title: Blender
rules.summary: Blender installations; each version installs into its own folder
rules.whatItIs: Blender program files. The installer creates a separate folder per version, so older versions remain unless uninstalled.
rules.whyBig: Each version is about 1 GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Blender stops working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall old Blender versions from Installed apps.

rules.title: Epic Games
rules.summary: Epic Games Launcher, Unreal Engine versions and Epic games
rules.whatItIs: Default location of the Epic Games Launcher, Unreal Engine installs (UE_x.y) and games from the Epic Games Store.
rules.whyBig: Unreal Engine versions are 30-60 GB each, and games are tens of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Games and engines stop working and the launcher may try to download them again.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games and engine versions from the Epic Games Launcher.

rules.title: Epic Games (x86)
rules.summary: Epic Games Launcher (older installs) and Epic games
rules.whatItIs: Older Epic Games Launcher installations put the launcher here.
rules.whyBig: The launcher and any games installed alongside it.
rules.ifDeleted: The launcher or games stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall through the Epic Games Launcher or Installed apps.

rules.title: Unreal Engine (launcher install)
rules.summary: An Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic launcher; remove it there
rules.whatItIs: One Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic Games Launcher, with editor binaries, source headers, content and platform support.
rules.whyBig: 30-60 GB per version, more with debug symbols and extra platforms.
rules.ifDeleted: Projects that use this version can no longer be opened with it.
rules.saferAlternative: In the Epic Games Launcher > Unreal Engine > Library, remove versions you no longer use, or deselect optional parts (Options) such as debug symbols.

rules.title: Epic launcher asset cache (VaultCache)
rules.summary: Downloaded Fab/Marketplace assets; safe to clear, downloaded again when needed
rules.whatItIs: Local cache of assets you downloaded from Fab or the Unreal Marketplace, kept so they can be added to projects without downloading again.
rules.whyBig: Each asset pack is hundreds of MB to tens of GB and stays after it has been added to a project.
rules.ifDeleted: Projects keep the assets already added to them. Adding an asset to another project needs a new download.
rules.saferAlternative: You can also change the vault cache location in the launcher's settings.

rules.title: Steam
rules.summary: Steam client and its default game library (steamapps)
rules.whatItIs: The Steam client. Its default library (steamapps) holds installed games, shader caches and Workshop content.
rules.whyBig: Games in steamapps\common are usually the bulk, often hundreds of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Steam and every game in its default library stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from Steam, or move them with Steam > Settings > Storage.

rules.title: Steam app cache
rules.summary: Steam's cache of app information and library data; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cached store, library and app information that Steam downloads. Clearing it is a standard Steam troubleshooting step.
rules.whyBig: Library artwork (librarycache) and HTTP cache grow over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Steam rebuilds it on next start. Quit Steam first.

rules.title: Steam depot manifests
rules.summary: Download manifests of Steam games; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Manifests that describe the files of each game version Steam downloaded.
rules.whyBig: Usually small, sometimes hundreds of MB after many updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Steam downloads manifests again when updating.

rules.title: Steam logs
rules.summary: Steam client logs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files of the Steam client.
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: Steam crash dumps
rules.summary: Crash dumps of Steam; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Crash dumps of the Steam client and its helper processes.
rules.whyBig: Repeated crashes add dumps.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: Steam user data
rules.summary: Your Steam settings, local cloud saves and screenshots
rules.whatItIs: Per-account Steam data: settings, controller configurations, local copies of Steam Cloud saves and screenshots (760\remote).
rules.whyBig: Screenshots and games that save locally through Steam can add GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Settings and screenshots are lost; saves that are not in Steam Cloud are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Manage screenshots from Steam's screenshot manager; keep the folder otherwise.

rules.title: Steam library folder
rules.summary: An additional Steam library with installed games
rules.whatItIs: A Steam library folder on this drive, created from Steam > Settings > Storage.
rules.whyBig: Games installed to this library.
rules.ifDeleted: The games in it stop working and Steam asks to download them again.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall or move games from Steam > Settings > Storage.

rules.title: Steam apps folder
rules.summary: Steam games, Workshop items, shader caches and downloads
rules.whatItIs: The content folder of a Steam library: installed games (common), Workshop items, shader caches, partial downloads and the app manifests that tell Steam what is installed.
rules.whyBig: Installed games are the bulk; shader caches and Workshop content add more.
rules.ifDeleted: Steam no longer sees the games in this library and offers to download them again.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from Steam, or move them with Steam > Settings > Storage.

rules.title: Installed Steam games
rules.summary: Installed Steam games; uninstall them from Steam
rules.whatItIs: One folder per installed Steam game.
rules.whyBig: Modern games are 20-150 GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: Steam marks the games as broken and downloads them again; saves are usually in the cloud, Documents or AppData.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from your Steam library (Manage > Uninstall).

rules.title: Steam shader pre-caching
rules.summary: Pre-compiled shaders for Steam games; safe to clear but games may stutter
rules.whatItIs: Shaders that Steam downloads or compiles ahead of time for your GPU (Shader Pre-Caching), plus Vulkan and OpenGL pipeline caches.
rules.whyBig: One folder per game; Vulkan and Proton games can have caches of several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Steam downloads or recompiles shaders, and games may stutter or load longer until the cache is rebuilt.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn off Shader Pre-Caching in Steam > Settings > Downloads if you do not want it.

rules.title: Steam partial downloads
rules.summary: Partially downloaded games and updates; deleting restarts those downloads
rules.whatItIs: Steam's staging area for game downloads and updates that are in progress or paused.
rules.whyBig: A paused large update can leave tens of GB here.
rules.ifDeleted: Downloads in progress start over. Quit Steam or pause downloads first.

rules.title: Steam temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files of Steam updates; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Temporary files Steam uses while updating games.
rules.whyBig: Interrupted updates leave files behind.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; quit Steam first.

rules.title: Steam Workshop content
rules.summary: Mods and items you subscribed to in the Steam Workshop
rules.whatItIs: Downloaded Workshop items (mods, maps, skins) for your games.
rules.whyBig: Popular mod collections can be many GB, and items of uninstalled games may remain.
rules.ifDeleted: Subscribed items are downloaded again while you stay subscribed.
rules.saferAlternative: Unsubscribe from Workshop items you do not use.

rules.title: Proton prefixes (Steam on Linux)
rules.summary: Windows environments for Proton games; often contain game saves
rules.whatItIs: Per-game Wine/Proton prefixes that Steam creates to run Windows games on Linux. Each one is a small Windows profile.
rules.whyBig: Each prefix is a few hundred MB, and prefixes of uninstalled games remain.
rules.ifDeleted: Games recreate their prefix, but saves and settings stored inside it are lost unless they are in Steam Cloud.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete prefixes only for games you uninstalled and whose saves are backed up.

rules.title: Steam app manifest
rules.summary: Tells Steam which game is installed in this library
rules.whatItIs: A small text file Steam keeps for each installed game in a library.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Steam no longer sees the game as installed.

rules.title: Battle.net app
rules.summary: Battle.net launcher program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of the Battle.net launcher.
rules.whyBig: A few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Battle.net stops working; installed games stay but cannot be launched or updated from it.

rules.title: Ubisoft Connect
rules.summary: Ubisoft Connect launcher; by default also holds games and local save copies
rules.whatItIs: The Ubisoft Connect launcher. By default games install into its games folder, and local copies of saves are kept in savegames.
rules.whyBig: Installed games are tens of GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: Ubisoft Connect and its games stop working; local saves not synced to the cloud are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from Ubisoft Connect.

rules.title: Ubisoft Connect saves
rules.summary: Local copies of your Ubisoft game saves
rules.whatItIs: Save games of Ubisoft titles, synced with Ubisoft's cloud when cloud saves are on.
rules.whyBig: Saves are usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Saves that are not in the cloud are lost.

rules.title: EA app and games
rules.summary: EA app (formerly Origin) and games installed with it
rules.whatItIs: The EA app and, depending on settings, games installed through it.
rules.whyBig: Games are tens of GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: The EA app and its games stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from the EA app.

rules.title: EA games
rules.summary: Games installed by the EA app
rules.whatItIs: Default install folder for games from the EA app.
rules.whyBig: Games are tens of GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: The games stop working and the EA app offers to download them again.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from the EA app.

rules.title: Riot Vanguard anti-cheat
rules.summary: Kernel-level anti-cheat for Riot games; uninstall it from Installed apps
rules.whatItIs: Riot Vanguard, the kernel-level anti-cheat required by VALORANT and League of Legends. It loads a driver at boot.
rules.whyBig: Small.
rules.ifDeleted: Riot games refuse to start, and a partially deleted boot driver can cause errors at start-up.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall 'Riot Vanguard' from Installed apps.

rules.title: Android Studio
rules.summary: Android Studio IDE program files
rules.whatItIs: Program files of Android Studio. The Android SDK and emulator images are stored separately in AppData\Local\Android\Sdk.
rules.whyBig: The IDE is 2-3 GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Android Studio stops working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall from Installed apps.

rules.title: Java runtimes and JDKs
rules.summary: Java runtimes and JDKs; old versions often remain
rules.whatItIs: Java runtime environments and development kits. Some updaters install a new version beside the old one.
rules.whyBig: Each JDK is 300 MB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs that need a removed Java version stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove old Java versions from Installed apps.
